events.name: Pendine Sands Hot Rod Races
events.blurb: The UK's premier vintage hot rod meeting, run by the Vintage Hot Rod Association on the historic firm sands of Pendine. Two days of speed runs with pre-1949 cars and bikes reaching over 130 mph; free for spectators outside the pits.

events.name: Pendine Sands Races
events.blurb: Running event held directly on the firm beach at Pendine, offering 5k, 10k, Half Marathon and Marathon distances on the famous land-speed-record sands.

events.name: Babs Land Speed Record Centenary
events.when: one-off centenary on 27 April 2026, with Babs on display at the Museum of Land Speed from May 2026
events.blurb: Special centenary celebration marking 100 years since J.G. Parry-Thomas set the world land speed record at Pendine Sands in 1926. The legendary car 'Babs' returns to the beach and goes on display at the Museum of Land Speed.

events.name: The Laugharne Weekend
events.blurb: An intimate literary and arts festival in the nearby town of Laugharne (about 7 km from Pendine), celebrating the legacy of Dylan Thomas with leftfield literature, music and comedy from Welsh and international artists.

events.name: Bedruthan Christmas Fayre
events.when: annually late November (Sat-Sun) at Bedruthan Hotel & Spa, Mawgan Porth; 2025 edition was 22-23 November, 2026 dates not yet confirmed
events.blurb: Annual craft and gift fair at the Bedruthan Hotel & Spa in Mawgan Porth, featuring art, ceramics, textiles, jewellery, homewares and local food and drink stalls.

events.name: St Eval Church Flower Festival
events.when: annually, normally the last weekend in June, at St Eval Parish Church (about 3 km from the beach)
events.blurb: Long-running community flower festival at the historic Grade I listed St Eval Church, with floral displays created by local volunteers and home-made refreshments.

events.name: Falcon Fest
events.when: annually in June at The Falcon Inn, St Mawgan (about 5 km away); a weekend of live music, cider, ales and street food in the pub garden
events.blurb: A weekend music and drink festival held in the garden of The Falcon Inn in the village of St Mawgan, with live bands, local ciders and ales, and street food.

events.name: Boardmasters Festival
events.when: annually in August at Watergate Bay and Fistral Beach, Newquay (Watergate Bay is roughly 6 km from the beach)
events.blurb: Cornwall's largest music and surf festival, held on the cliffs above Watergate Bay near Newquay, with a major line-up of music acts plus surfing and skating competitions.

events.name: Bedruthan Live (RE:SET summer music series)
events.when: summer season at Bedruthan Steps campsite, Mawgan Porth, with an outdoor live music series alongside wellness workshops
events.blurb: Summer programme of outdoor live music at the Bedruthan Steps campsite in Mawgan Porth, accompanied by yoga, sound baths and wellness sessions in the tipi field.

events.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Cayman Cookout
events.when: annually mid-January at The Ritz-Carlton on Seven Mile Beach; 2026 edition 14-18 January
events.blurb: A world-renowned food and wine festival held at The Ritz-Carlton, Grand Cayman, directly on Seven Mile Beach, with celebrity-chef cooking demonstrations, tastings and beachside dinners.

events.name: Flowers Sea Swim
events.when: annually in June along Seven Mile Beach; 2026 edition 13 June
events.blurb: A one-mile open-water swim race along Seven Mile Beach drawing over 1,000 competitors, from recreational swimmers to Olympic-level athletes.

events.name: One Cayman Carnival (Batabano & CayMAS)
events.when: annually in May; 2026 unified Road Parade on Saturday 23 May (Junior Parade 2 May), through George Town ending at Public Beach on Seven Mile Beach
events.blurb: Grand Cayman's national carnival, in 2026 uniting Batabano and CayMAS into One Cayman Carnival, with soca music, mas bands, costumes and a road parade ending at Seven Mile Beach Public Beach.

events.name: Pirates Week Festival
events.when: annually in November (typically the second week)
events.blurb: The Cayman Islands' signature maritime-heritage festival featuring a mock pirate invasion, parades, street dancing, local food, sports, Heritage Days and fireworks across Grand Cayman.

events.name: Cayman Art Week
events.blurb: A week-long curated programme of gallery tours, open studios and exhibitions celebrating local visual artists across the Cayman Islands.

events.name: Cayman Islands Agricultural Show
events.when: annually on Ash Wednesday; 2026 edition 18 February
events.blurb: A long-running agricultural fair showcasing the islands' livestock, produce and local food alongside live music and arts and crafts.

events.name: Aberavon Beach Festival
events.blurb: An annual community festival on Aberavon Beach featuring live music, tribute acts, market stalls, beach games, a kids' festival and wellness activities over a summer weekend.

events.name: Aberavon Super Sprint Triathlon
events.blurb: A community super-sprint triathlon organised by Port Talbot Harriers, with a 400m pool swim, a 10km bike course and a 3km run along Aberavon Beach.

events.name: Aberavon Surf Lifesaving Club Junior Aquathlon
events.blurb: A junior swim-and-run aquathlon held on Aberavon Beach, run by Aberavon Surf Lifesaving Club in conjunction with Port Talbot Harriers and Welsh Triathlon.

events.name: Aberdeen Festival of the Sea
events.blurb: A citywide celebration of Aberdeen's maritime heritage with around 40 free and paid events; the Beach Esplanade hosts headline elements including the parade of sail and a grand finale. It runs in July, coinciding with the Tall Ships Races visit to the harbour.

events.name: Aberdeen parkrun
events.blurb: A free, timed 5km run, jog or walk held every Saturday morning along the Beach Esplanade at Aberdeen Beach. Open to all and run by volunteers.

events.name: City of Aberdeen Baker Hughes 10k Running Festival
events.blurb: A long-established 10k road race (with 2k and wheelchair options) based around Aberdeen Beach and harbour, starting on Beach Boulevard and running along the Beach Esplanade past the Beach Ballroom. First held in 1987.

events.name: Fishguard Folk Festival
events.blurb: A mostly free folk music festival held at venues across Fishguard including St Mary's Church and Theatr Gwaun, with concerts, sessions, workshops, ceilidh/twmpath, dance displays and guided walks. The 2026 line-up includes Alaw, Cynefin and Three Daft Monkeys.

events.name: Fishguard Multi-Sport Festival
events.blurb: A weekend of endurance running races around Fishguard, including a Half Marathon, a scenic 10K and a 5K aimed at first-time racers.

events.name: ABBAGwaun Festival
events.blurb: A three-day ABBA-themed festival in Fishguard (Abergwaun) featuring film screenings, live music, ABBA bingo, costume competitions and a parade.

events.name: Fishguard Bay Ocean Race
events.blurb: An annual downwind paddle/ski sea race starting at Goodwick Parrog and crossing roughly 17km of open water to finish on Newport Sands, now in its second decade.

events.name: The Big Retreat Festival
events.blurb: An annual wellbeing and music festival set in the village of Lawrenny within the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, combining live music, food, talks and outdoor experiences over the May bank holiday weekend.

events.name: Pembroke Music Festival
events.blurb: An annual six-day music festival anchored at Pembroke Town Hall, the nearest sizeable town to Barafundle Bay, featuring concerts and performances across the autumn week.

events.name: Fishguard Folk Festival
events.when: annually over the late May bank holiday (2026: 22-26 May)
events.blurb: A traditional folk music festival held across venues in Fishguard, Pembrokeshire, over the May bank holiday weekend with concerts, dancing and food.

events.name: Dartmouth Triathlon
events.blurb: An annual sprint and standard-distance triathlon organised by Sportiva Events, with the sea swim leg held in the waters of Blackpool Sands followed by a bike ride via Slapton and a run up Blackpool Valley. Open sea swims of 750m, 1500m and 3km are also held the evening before.

events.name: Tribal Clash
events.blurb: A two-day team fitness competition held on a purpose-built arena on Blackpool Sands beach, where teams of six tackle surprise functional challenges including running, swimming, hauling and carrying. It is one of the beach's flagship recurring events.

events.name: Apres Sea Saturdays
events.when: Saturday afternoons through the summer season
events.blurb: Recurring summer beach parties at Blackpool Sands with live music and DJs on Saturday afternoons, alongside the beach's regular Saturday morning live music and breakfast club sessions.

events.name: Pembroke Festival
events.blurb: A multi-day arts and community festival in the historic town of Pembroke, the nearest town to Broad Haven South, featuring live music, town-wide arts events, workshops, crafts and family activities.

events.name: Pembroke Music Festival
events.blurb: A competitive music festival held over several days at Pembroke Town Hall, with classes in singing, piano, strings and choir, masterclasses and a finale concert.

events.name: The Big Retreat Festival
events.blurb: A wellbeing, music and food festival held at Lawrenny within the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, combining live music, wellbeing sessions, food, talks and outdoor experiences.

events.name: Rye Bay Scallop Week
events.when: annually late February to early March (2026: 21 Feb - 1 Mar)
events.blurb: A week-long celebration of the local Rye Bay scallop catch with tasting menus, cooking classes, live music and wine pairings across the town's restaurants. Now in its 22nd year, it is one of East Sussex's most popular annual food events.

events.name: Rye International Jazz & Blues Festival
events.when: annually over the August Bank Holiday (2026: 28-31 Aug)
events.blurb: A boutique music festival held in venues across Rye, including St Mary's Church, featuring jazz, blues, soul, R&B, funk and world music with a mix of ticketed and free performances over the August Bank Holiday weekend.

events.name: Camber Kite Week
events.blurb: An annual kitesurfing gathering on the wide flats of Camber Sands organised by the local kitesurfing community, combining kitesurfing sessions with music, food and beachside camping.

events.name: Rye Arts Festival
events.blurb: Founded in 1972 and regarded as one of Britain's top small arts festivals, it offers a mix of musical, literary and theatrical events across the historic town of Rye near Camber Sands.

camp-bay-gibraltar.town: Gibraltar (Camp Bay is on the south-west tip of the Rock of Gibraltar)

events.name: Summer Nights - Summer Reggae Jam at Camp Bay
events.blurb: Camp Bay beach hosts a free open-air Reggae Jam as part of Gibraltar's Summer Nights programme, with live acts, sunset dancing and food stalls. In 2025 it ran on 7 August from 6:30pm to 11:00pm.

events.name: Gibraltar National Day
events.blurb: Gibraltar's biggest annual celebration, when the territory dresses in red and white for street parties, concerts and the release of thousands of red-and-white balloons. It commemorates the 1967 sovereignty referendum.

events.name: Gibraltar International Dance Festival
events.blurb: The 24th edition of Gibraltar's international dance festival runs 3-7 March 2026 at the John Mackintosh Hall Theatre, featuring over 250 dancers from Gibraltar, England, Italy, Spain and Albania.

events.name: Gibraltar Music Festival
events.blurb: Gibraltar's flagship music festival, traditionally held at the Alameda Botanical Gardens, drawing major international acts each year.

events.name: Walrus Dip (Boxing Day Swim)
events.blurb: An annual Boxing Day charity sea swim held on the dune-backed sands of Cefn Sidan beach at Pembrey Country Park, with fancy dress encouraged. The dip starts around 10:45am and attracts hundreds of swimmers and spectators.

events.name: Wales National Armed Forces Day 2026
events.blurb: Carmarthenshire hosts the Wales National Armed Forces Day 2026 at Pembrey Country Park, a family-friendly event for the public to show support for the Armed Forces community.

events.name: Pembrey Summer Feastival
events.blurb: A coastal food and music weekend at Pembrey Country Park, set between the woodland and the eight-mile Cefn Sidan beach, featuring nomadic cooks, family entertainment and a live music stage.

events.name: b-side Festival
events.blurb: A four-day contemporary arts festival staged across the Isle of Portland, featuring site-specific artworks, performances and creative encounters inspired by the island's landscape and community. The 2026 edition is themed 'That Other Place'.

events.name: Criccieth Festival (Gŵyl Criccieth)
events.blurb: An annual arts festival founded in 1990 celebrating music, culture and local heritage in Criccieth, featuring classical and folk concerts, literary talks and guided walks set against the backdrop of Cardigan Bay. It runs for around a week in mid-June.

events.name: Criccieth Food Slam
events.when: annually mid-June, closing weekend of the Criccieth Festival
events.blurb: A food festival held on the Criccieth esplanade beside the beach at the end of the Criccieth Festival week, with street food, beer, wine, live music and arts and crafts stalls.

events.name: Criccieth Fair and the Big Fair
events.blurb: Criccieth holds two traditional annual fairs dating back to the Victorian era, the first on 23 May and the larger 'Big Fair' on 29 June, with a funfair in the town.

events.name: Crosby parkrun
events.blurb: A free, timed 5km community run held every Saturday morning, starting near Crosby Leisure Centre and running along the promenade and Crosby Beach past Antony Gormley's 'Another Place' iron men sculptures.

events.name: Antony Gormley's 'Another Place'
events.blurb: One hundred life-size cast-iron figures by sculptor Antony Gormley are spread along almost 3km of Crosby Beach facing out to sea, a permanent free public artwork and the area's best-known visitor draw.

events.name: Carloway Agricultural Show and Highland Games
events.blurb: The longest-established agricultural show on the Isle of Lewis, running since 1911, held in the crofting township of Carloway just inland from Dail Mor beach. It features livestock judging (Lewis and Harris championships), Highland Games, a dog show, equestrian and piping competitions.

events.name: HebCelt (Hebridean Celtic Festival)
events.blurb: A long-running Celtic and folk music festival held in Stornoway on the Isle of Lewis since 1996, the island's biggest annual cultural event. The 2026 edition runs 15-18 July with headliners including The Saw Doctors, Manran and The Mary Wallopers.

events.name: Gibraltar National Day
events.blurb: Gibraltar's main national celebration commemorating the 1967 sovereignty referendum, centred on Casemates Square with a Freedom of the City ceremony, live music, family activities and an evening fireworks display.

events.name: Gibraltar Music Festival
events.blurb: Gibraltar's flagship open-air music festival held at the Alameda Botanical Gardens, drawing international headline acts each year.

events.name: Gibraltar Spring Festival
events.when: annually over three weeks between May and June
events.blurb: A multi-week celebration marking the start of summer with dance shows, art exhibitions, theatrical performances and concerts, concluding with a food festival.

events.name: Brixham Pirate Festival
events.when: annually early-May bank holiday weekend (2026: 2-4 May)
events.blurb: A free pirate-themed festival centred on Brixham Harbour over the early May bank holiday weekend, with costumed crowds, live music, street entertainment and family activities. Brixham is the nearest town to Elberry Cove.

events.name: English Riviera Airshow
events.blurb: A free annual airshow over Torbay centred on Paignton Green, with aerial displays confirmed to include the Red Arrows, Typhoon and Battle of Britain Memorial Flight. 2026 marks the show's 10th anniversary.

events.name: Paddle UK SUPER Festival & SUP World Cup
events.blurb: The English Riviera hosts the Paddle UK SUPER Festival together with a Stand-Up Paddleboard World Cup, bringing paddle sport competition and participation events to the Torbay coast.

events.name: Paignton Festival
events.blurb: A nine-day free community festival in Paignton (formerly the Torbay Carnival) featuring family entertainment, the Riviera Classic Car Show and a funfair. Paignton, with its Broadsands beach, is the access point for Elberry Cove.

events.name: Prestatyn Carnival
events.when: annually on the third Saturday in July (2026-07-18)
events.blurb: One of the longest-established carnivals in North Wales, run by the Prestatyn Carnival Association. The day features a grand parade through the High Street followed by a carnival field on Bastion Road with arenas, a funfair, dog shows, live entertainment and craft and trade stalls.

events.name: Prestatyn Winter Fest
events.when: annually in late November (Christmas lights switch-on)
events.blurb: A two-day Christmas festival on Prestatyn High Street organised around the town's Christmas lights switch-on, featuring a Christmas market, food and drink stalls, live music, funfair rides and an ice rink. First held in 2023 and now an annual tradition.

events.name: Boardmasters Festival
events.blurb: Cornwall's largest surf and music festival, with the surf competition, skate ramp and Surf Village staged at Fistral Beach while the music programme runs at nearby Watergate Bay. It draws up to 58,000 visitors each August.

events.name: Boardmasters Open (YETI Pro QS 4,000)
events.blurb: A World Surf League Qualifying Series surf contest held in the waves at Fistral Beach, upgraded for 2026 to a QS 4,000 with YETI as presenting sponsor, ranking among the top European qualifying events.

events.name: SLSGB National Surf Life Saving Championships
events.blurb: Surf Life Saving Great Britain holds its national surf championships at Fistral Beach, drawing 260-plus competitors racing surf skis, paddleboards and kayaks. Newquay Surf Life Saving Club is based within the Fistral surf complex.

events.name: Formby Festival
events.when: annually, third weekend of July (no event in 2026; return planned 16-18 July 2027)
events.blurb: Formby's long-running community summer festival of food, drink, music and entertainment, traditionally held on the third weekend of July. It is not running in 2026 (cancelled due to rising costs), with organisers planning to revive it on 16-18 July 2027.

events.name: Welsh National Surfing Championships
events.blurb: The Welsh Surfing Federation's flagship contest, frequently held at Freshwater West, crowns Welsh national champions across multiple age and gender categories on the beach's Atlantic swells.

events.name: Wilkinson Sword Inter-Club Surf Contest
events.blurb: A long-running Welsh inter-club surfing competition staged at Freshwater West, contested between Pembrokeshire surf clubs for the prestigious Wilkinson Sword trophy.

events.name: Pembroke Festival
events.blurb: A multi-day community arts festival in nearby Pembroke featuring live music, town-wide arts events, workshops, crafts and family activities.

events.name: Paignton Festival (Torbay Carnival)
events.blurb: A long-running, mostly free community festival in Paignton featuring children's entertainment, sporting events, a funfair and the Spinning Wheel Carnival Procession (29 July 2026). It has run for over 100 years.

events.name: English Riviera Airshow (Torbay Airshow)
events.blurb: Free airshow with flying displays over Torbay from Paignton Green, including the RAF Red Arrows, RAF Typhoon and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight.

events.name: English Riviera Walking Festival
events.blurb: A two-week festival of guided walks across the English Riviera and South Devon, exploring local coast and countryside with knowledgeable guides.

events.name: Geopark Festival
events.blurb: A family-oriented UNESCO Global Geopark festival with creative and exploratory activities, centred in part on the Geoplay Park at Paignton seafront.

events.name: Festival for the Ocean
events.when: annually early June (around World Oceans Day, 8 June)
events.blurb: Free family festival held directly on Gyllyngvase Beach to celebrate the sea and marine conservation, featuring giant marine creatures, hands-on activities and environmental learning. Organised by Falmouth Town Council on the eve of World Oceans Day.

events.name: Falmouth Week
events.blurb: The largest sailing regatta in the south west of England, with more than 400 yachts racing in Falmouth Bay over eight days, plus shoreside entertainment, markets and the Pink Wig Mermaid March. Gyllyngvase Beach is one of the prime spots to watch the racing.

events.name: Falmouth International Sea Shanty Festival
events.blurb: A free three-day maritime music festival drawing tens of thousands of visitors and more than 70 shanty groups from around the world to venues across Falmouth town and harbour.

events.name: Falmouth Oyster Festival
events.blurb: A four-day celebration marking the start of the native oyster dredging season, with cookery demonstrations, live entertainment and locally caught seafood, held in Falmouth's Events Square.

events.name: Mevagissey Feast Week
events.when: annually late June to early July (2026: 28 June - 4 July)
events.blurb: Cornwall's longest-running festival (since 1754), celebrating St Peter, patron saint of fishermen, in the harbour village of Mevagissey near Hemmick Beach. The free week-long event features Fish Sunday with fresh fish on the quay, live music, flora dances, a raft race, fete, carnival and fireworks.

events.name: Mevagissey Shanty Festival
events.when: annually mid-October (2026: 16-18 October, Gala Night 15 October)
events.blurb: An annual weekend celebration of maritime sea shanty singing and local fishing heritage held across the harbour pubs and venues of Mevagissey, the nearest town to Hemmick Beach.

events.name: Gorran Haven Gig Regatta
events.blurb: A community pilot-gig rowing regatta centred on Gorran Haven beach, the nearest village to Hemmick Beach, alongside a harbour society gala day and street market.

events.name: Gorran Haven New Year's Day Charity Swim
events.blurb: The Gorran Haven rowing club organises a charity New Year's Day swim off the quay, following the village hall's New Year's Eve fireworks over the harbour.

events.name: Wells Carnival
events.when: annually early August (2026: 31 July - 9 August, Carnival Day 8 August)
events.blurb: A traditional seaside carnival held in Wells-next-the-Sea for over 100 years, with a week of family events culminating in a Carnival Day procession of floats and fancy dress, plus sandcastle and town crier competitions and the crowning of the Carnival Royals.

events.name: Outlaw Holkham Triathlon Weekend (Outlaw Half Holkham)
events.blurb: An endurance sport weekend in the grounds of the Holkham estate next to the beach, featuring the popular Outlaw Half middle-distance triathlon along with a 10km run and kids' races.

events.name: North Norfolk Food and Drink Festival
events.blurb: A free two-day celebration of regional produce held in the Walled Garden at Holkham Hall, with more than 60 local producers selling meats, vegetables, beers, chocolates and other North Norfolk fare.

events.name: Ventnor Fringe Festival
events.blurb: The Isle of Wight's multi-award-winning arts festival, featuring over 130 shows of theatre, comedy, cabaret, circus and music staged in unusual venues around Ventnor's seafront and town.

events.name: Ventnor Carnival Week (Grand Carnival & Fireworks)
events.when: annually mid-August (2026: 8-15 August, Grand Carnival 15 August)
events.blurb: A week of community carnival events along Ventnor's seafront culminating in the Grand Carnival procession and fireworks display. The week also includes a Children's Carnival and lantern parade.

events.name: Ventnor Pirate Festival
events.when: annually mid-August during Carnival Week (2026: 12-15 August)
events.blurb: A family-friendly four-day pirate-themed festival held along Ventnor seafront during Carnival Week, with live music, fancy dress and seaside entertainment.

events.name: Ventnor Illuminated Carnival
events.blurb: A winter illuminated evening carnival procession through Ventnor, a separate seasonal companion to the summer carnival week.

events.name: Grey Seal Pupping Season at Horsey Beach
events.when: annually late October to February (peak November-January)
events.blurb: Each winter thousands of grey seals haul out onto Horsey Beach to give birth, with over 3,500 pups born between Horsey and Winterton in the 2025/2026 season. Volunteers from the Friends of Horsey Seals manage viewing from the dunes and designated platforms during the breeding season.

events.name: Classic Car and Vintage Vehicle Show and Tell
events.blurb: Poppylands Tea Room at Horsey hosts an annual Classic Car and Vintage Vehicle Show and Tell, displaying classic and vintage vehicles near the beach. It marks one of the seasonal events in the Horsey area.

events.name: Gower Festival
events.when: annually late June to mid-July (2026: 29 June - 12 July)
events.blurb: A long-running classical music festival held across the historic churches and intimate venues of the Gower Peninsula. The 2026 edition runs from 29 June to 12 July, marking the festival's 50th anniversary fortnight.

events.name: Gower Walking Festival
events.blurb: An annual programme of guided walks celebrating the coast and countryside of the Gower Peninsula, including routes along the south Gower coast near Port Eynon and Horton. The 2026 festival runs from 5 to 13 September.

events.name: Gower Folk Festival
events.when: annually second weekend of June (2026: 12-14 June)
events.blurb: A small, volunteer-run, dog-friendly folk music festival held at Weobley Castle Farm in a coastal setting on the Gower Peninsula, with on-site camping. The 2026 edition takes place 12-14 June.

events.name: Port Eynon & South Gower Coast History Walk (Glamorgan History Walks Festival)
events.blurb: A guided 7-mile coastal history walk starting at Port Eynon, just along the bay from Horton Beach, run as part of the Glamorgan History Walks Festival. Scheduled for 17 May 2026 at 2:00pm.

events.name: Wilkinson Sword Welsh Inter-Clubs Surfing Championships
events.blurb: The Welsh Surfing Federation's most coveted trophy, contested annually since 1980 by Welsh surf clubs. Langland Bay is the home break of Langland Board Riders (2026 winners) and has hosted the contest, which rotates to the previous winner's beach.

events.name: Mumbles Triathlon (Mumbles Multi Sport Festival)
events.blurb: An annual triathlon held in Mumbles near Langland Bay, with Olympic and Sprint distances featuring an enclosed sea swim off Mumbles Bay plus cycle and run legs around Swansea Bay. Part of the Mumbles Multi Sport Festival.

events.name: Ironman 70.3 Swansea
events.blurb: A half-distance Ironman triathlon held in Swansea Bay, with the swim staged in the bay close to the Gower beaches including Langland Bay.

events.name: Marloes and St Brides Summer Fete
events.when: annually in early August (usually the first Thursday)
events.blurb: A traditional summer fete held in the grounds of St Brides Castle near Marloes, raising funds for the Marloes and St. Brides churches. Features stalls of cakes, books and home produce, games such as skittles and a coconut shy, refreshments and live singing.

events.name: Pendine Sands Hot Rod Races (VHRA)
events.blurb: The Vintage Hot Rod Association's annual beach races on Pendine Sands, the beach immediately adjoining Marros Sands. Pre-1949 hot rods and customs race a half-mile run-up over the firm sand; spectating is free and open to the public.

events.name: Pendine Sands Races (5k/10k/Half/Marathon/Ultra)
events.blurb: A series of running races held on the flat expanse of Pendine Sands, ranging from 5k up to a marathon and ultra distance, with the entire course run along the beach.

events.name: Land Speed Record Centenary - Babs returns to Pendine Sands
events.blurb: The legendary land speed record car Babs returns to Pendine Sands to mark the centenary of J.G. Parry-Thomas's 1926 world land speed record, organised by the Babs Trust with Pendine Community Council and the National Motor Museum of Wales.

events.name: Blue Bird Land Speed Record 100th Anniversary
events.blurb: Malcolm Campbell's Sunbeam 350hp Blue Bird returns to Pendine on the 100th anniversary of its 150mph land speed record, on display outside the Museum of Land Speed from 10am to 5pm with engineers planning a beach photoshoot.

events.name: English Riviera Airshow
events.blurb: Free annual airshow over Torbay featuring aerial displays from classic and modern aircraft, viewable from Torquay and Paignton seafronts.

events.name: ICF Stand Up Paddling (SUP) World Cup
events.blurb: The International Canoe Federation stages a major Stand Up Paddling World Cup on the English Riviera, the first event of this scale in the UK.

events.name: English Riviera Walking Festival
events.blurb: Annual festival of guided walks across the coastline and woodland of the English Riviera, including the South West Coast Path past Babbacombe and Oddicombe.

events.name: International Agatha Christie Festival
events.blurb: Annual festival celebrating Torquay-born author Agatha Christie, with talks, walks, films and performances across Torquay, Paignton and Brixham.

events.name: English Riviera UNESCO Global Geopark Festival
events.blurb: Annual festival of walks, workshops and exhibitions exploring the geology and natural heritage of the English Riviera Geopark.

paul-beach.town: Paul (near Mousehole and Newlyn, Penzance, Cornwall)

events.name: Tom Bawcock's Eve
events.blurb: Annual festival in nearby Mousehole honouring legendary fisherman Tom Bawcock, who braved a storm to bring back a catch and save the village from famine. The famous Mousehole harbour Christmas lights shine, a lantern procession winds through the village, and stargazy pie is served at the Ship Inn.

events.name: Mousehole Harbour Christmas Lights
events.blurb: Iconic illuminated displays strung around Mousehole harbour, a Cornish Christmas tradition begun in 1963. The lights are switched on in mid-December and run until around the first week of January.

events.name: Newlyn Fish Festival
events.blurb: A family-friendly celebration of Newlyn's fishing heritage on the harbourside, with market stalls, culinary demonstrations, live music and exhibitions. Held on the August Bank Holiday Monday.

events.name: Golowan Festival & Mazey Day
events.when: annually in late June; 2026 festival 19-28 June, Mazey Day 27 June
events.blurb: Penzance's midsummer arts and culture festival with parades, live music, street performers and makers' markets, culminating in the spectacular Mazey Day procession when the town centre becomes a street party.

pedn-vounder.town: Porthcurno (nearest village; Treen also adjacent), West Cornwall

events.name: Minack Theatre Performance Season
events.when: annually April to October (2026 season opens 3 April)
events.blurb: The open-air Minack Theatre, carved into the cliffs directly above Porthcurno Bay beside Pedn Vounder, runs a full performance season each year featuring plays, musicals, opera and live music. The 2026 season opens on 3 April with 'Giants' and runs through October.

events.name: Porthcurno Christmas Day Swim
events.blurb: Each Christmas morning locals and visitors gather at neighbouring Porthcurno beach for a festive dip in the Atlantic, often in fancy dress. Porthcurno is the cove adjoining Pedn Vounder, reachable on a low tide.

events.name: The du Maurier Fowey Literary Festival
events.blurb: Cornwall's longest-running literary festival, held in Fowey in honour of author Daphne du Maurier who lived nearby. It features authors, speakers, musicians and artists across venues in the town.

events.name: Fowey Royal Regatta and Carnival Week
events.when: annually the third week of August (2026: 16-22 August)
events.blurb: One of Britain's best-loved sailing regattas, running since 1819, with yacht and pilot gig races, harbour swims, a carnival procession, live music and fireworks in Fowey harbour. Readymoney Cove sits at the harbour mouth where regatta water events take place.

events.name: Bude Jazz Festival
events.blurb: A long-running four-day jazz festival in Bude, the nearest town to Sandymouth Beach, featuring traditional and New Orleans jazz with dozens of performances, bands and an opening parade across the town.

events.name: Bude Literary Festival
events.blurb: An annual literary festival held in Bude with author talks, readings and workshops over several days in May.

events.name: St Piran's Day Walk
events.blurb: An annual celebration of Cornwall's patron saint, with a community walk starting from Bude Surf Life Saving Club at Summerleaze Beach.

events.name: Bude Carnival
events.blurb: A traditional Cornish town carnival held annually in Bude, featuring a procession and community festivities.

events.name: Croyde Ocean Triathlon
events.blurb: An ocean-swim triathlon held on the North Devon coast near Saunton Sands, with the swim leg at nearby Putsborough Sands followed by road bike and off-road coastal run stages. All profit goes to charity.

events.name: Edward Capern Festival
events.blurb: An annual festival in Heanton Punchardon near Braunton commemorating the local Victorian 'Postman Poet' Edward Capern, featuring poetry, art, displays and choral music inspired by his work. The 2026 edition runs 4-5 June with a £500 poetry award.

events.name: Devon Street Food Festival
events.when: annually in July at Braunton Recreation Grounds
events.blurb: A street-food festival held at Braunton Recreation Grounds, the village nearest Saunton Sands, with food vendors, drink and live entertainment over a summer weekend.

events.name: Bermuda Day Parade
events.blurb: Bermuda's signature national holiday and the unofficial start of summer, marked by a colourful parade along Front Street in Hamilton with majorettes, Gombey dancers, floats and the traditional Bermuda Day half-marathon. The 2026 parade starts at 12:30 PM.

events.name: Cup Match Cricket Classic
events.blurb: A two-day public-holiday cricket classic coinciding with Emancipation Day and Mary Prince Day, with the venue alternating between the Somerset and St George's clubs; the 2026 match is hosted by Somerset Cricket Club. It is one of Bermuda's biggest annual cultural and sporting events.

events.name: Bermuda Carnival (Carnival in Bermuda)
events.when: 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-15 (annually around National Heroes Weekend in June)
events.blurb: A six-day Caribbean-style carnival of fetes, soca music, J'ouvert and the costumed Revel de Road street parade, culminating on National Heroes Day. It is one of the island's largest annual celebrations.

events.name: Chubb Bermuda Triangle Challenge
events.blurb: An annual three-day running festival based out of Hamilton featuring the Butterfield Mile, a 10K, and the PwC Bermuda Marathon and Half Marathon, with a combined Full Triangle Challenge over the weekend.

st-mary-s-bay.town: St Mary's Bay (Romney Marsh), Kent — nearest towns Dymchurch and New Romney

events.name: Day of Syn Festival, Dymchurch
events.when: biennially over the August Bank Holiday weekend (next: 28-31 August 2026)
events.blurb: A free community festival in neighbouring Dymchurch celebrating the fictional smuggling vicar Dr Syn (the Scarecrow), with costumed parades, mummers, morris dancers, a sea-wall lantern parade and fireworks. It is one of the largest free events in Kent.

events.name: New Romney Country Fayre
events.when: annually in late July (2026: Saturday 25 July)
events.blurb: Billed as the largest free community event on Romney Marsh, held in nearby New Romney with a carnival parade, two entertainment arenas, over 100 stalls of local produce and family activities.

events.name: JAM on the Marsh
events.blurb: An annual arts and music festival across Romney Marsh, with concerts and performances at venues including St Nicholas' Church in nearby New Romney and other historic Marsh churches. The 2026 programme focuses on the music of France and the influence of jazz on classical music.

the-baths.town: Spanish Town (The Valley), Virgin Gorda, British Virgin Islands

events.name: Virgin Gorda Easter Festival
events.when: annually over Easter weekend (Sat-Mon); in 2026 April 4-6
events.blurb: Virgin Gorda's main cultural celebration, held in Spanish Town over the Easter weekend with a food fair, Festival Village live performances, calypso, fungi music and the highlight Easter Monday street parade.

events.name: BVI Emancipation Festival
events.when: annually late July to early August; in 2026 July 25 - August 8
events.blurb: The British Virgin Islands' nationwide two-week celebration of emancipation from slavery (since 1954), with parades, food fairs, fungi music, pageants and street jams; Emancipation Monday is the centerpiece. Celebrated across the territory including Virgin Gorda.

events.name: Taste of Virgin Gorda
events.when: annually (part of BVI Food Fete); in 2026 February 28
events.blurb: A signature culinary celebration held at the Virgin Gorda Yacht Harbour in Spanish Town, where local chefs and restaurants serve small-plate dishes; part of the BVI Food Fete series.

events.name: BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival
events.blurb: A major Caribbean sailing regatta based at Nanny Cay, Tortola, whose race courses tour the British Virgin Islands including the waters around Virgin Gorda. A bucket-list event drawing international crews each spring.

events.name: Wirral Wader Festival
events.blurb: A community wildlife festival based at the Wirral Country Park visitor centre at Thurstaston, with stalls, children's activities, high-tide wader watches and guided coastal walks. It was the first event of its kind in the UK, launched in 2015 with Wader Quest.

events.name: Wirral Earth Festival (Earthfest)
events.blurb: An annual people-and-planet-friendly festival held on St Bridget's school field in nearby West Kirby, featuring local musicians, food and drink, arts and crafts, and information on sustainable living. Organised by Transition Town West Kirby.

events.name: Wirral Walking Festival
events.blurb: A month-long celebration of the Wirral peninsula's footpaths and coastal scenery, with guided walks across the area including the coast near Thurstaston and the Wirral Way.

traeth-bychan.town: Moelfre / Marian-Glas, Anglesey (between Benllech and Moelfre)

events.name: Anglesey Offshore Dinghy & Catamaran Race (AODR)
events.blurb: A long-distance dinghy and catamaran race hosted by Red Wharf Bay Sailing & Watersports Club, which is based at Traeth Bychan beach. The course runs between Beaumaris and Traeth Bychan via the Menai Strait and Puffin Island, with the start/finish at Traeth Bychan.

events.name: Moelfre Lifeboat Day
events.blurb: A major annual RNLI fundraising day in the nearby village of Moelfre, featuring a lifeboat launch and display, rescue helicopter demonstrations, stalls, food, music and family entertainment around Beach Road and the Seawatch Centre.

events.name: Anglesey Oyster & Welsh Produce Festival
events.blurb: An annual food festival celebrating Anglesey oysters and Welsh produce, held on the Isle of Anglesey where Traeth Bychan is located.

events.name: Fèis Bharraigh
events.blurb: An annual Gaelic arts and culture festival held on the Isle of Barra and Vatersay since 1981, offering tuition in traditional Scottish music, instruments, drama and Gaelic language alongside community events.

events.name: Barralive Music Festival
events.blurb: An island music festival on the Isle of Barra featuring live music and local talent, bringing together the community for a summer celebration.

events.name: Barra Produce Show
events.blurb: A long-running annual agricultural and produce show on the Isle of Barra, celebrating local horticulture, baking and crafts, including the island's well-known potato competition.

events.name: Zennor Feast
events.when: annually, Sunday closest to 10 May, plus following feast week
events.blurb: Zennor's traditional parish feast honouring St Senara, held on the Sunday nearest 10 May and followed by a community 'feast week' with a Monday concert of local talent, a rounders match between East and West, clay pigeon shoot, barn dances and quiz nights. Treen and Treen Cove lie within Zennor parish.

events.name: St Ives Food & Drink Festival
events.blurb: A free three-day beach food festival on the sands of Porthminster Beach in St Ives, the nearest town to Treen Cove, featuring top chef demonstrations, live music and artisan food and drink. In 2026 it runs 15-17 May.

events.name: St Ives September Festival
events.blurb: A two-week arts and music festival in St Ives, the nearest town to Treen Cove, blending live music, art, poetry, talks, theatre and film across venues including St Ives Theatre and the Guildhall, with free street entertainment. In 2026 it runs 12-26 September.

events.name: Mevagissey Feast Week
events.when: annually late June / early July (2026: 28 June – 4 July)
events.blurb: Cornwall's longest-running festival (since 1754), held in the nearby fishing village of Mevagissey to honour St Peter, patron saint of fishermen. The free week-long event features Fish Sunday on the harbour quay, live music, parades, raft races, flora dances and a fireworks display.

events.name: Gorran Haven Regatta
events.blurb: A community seaside regatta in Gorran Haven, the village closest to Vault Beach, featuring pilot gig rowing races, boat events, music and family activities around the harbour and beach.

events.name: Gorran Haven New Year's Day Charity Swim
events.blurb: A New Year's Day charity sea swim organised by the village rowing club at Gorran Haven, following New Year's Eve fireworks off the quay.

events.name: Borth Carnival
events.blurb: An annual seaside village carnival held on the first Friday in August on the Uppingham Playing Fields in Borth, the nearest coastal village to Wallog, featuring a parade, activities and refreshments.

events.name: Borth Scarecrow Festival (Borthfest / Gwylborth)
events.when: annually, late May bank holiday weekend
events.blurb: Organised by Borth Arts, this community festival sees scarecrows displayed across the village of Borth over the spring bank holiday weekend, alongside the wider Borthfest celebration of music and arts.

events.name: Musicfest Aberystwyth
events.blurb: Aberystwyth's annual eight-day international music festival, running since 1987, combining world-class concerts, a summer music school and free activities. The 2026 edition takes place 18-25 July.

events.name: Aberystwyth and Ceredigion County Show
events.blurb: One of the largest one-day agricultural shows in mid-Wales, held on the second Saturday of June near Aberystwyth, with livestock, crafts and food. The 2026 show is on 13 June.

events.name: Weymouth Beach Summer Fireworks
events.blurb: A series of summer firework displays launched from a boat in Weymouth Bay opposite the town's sandy beach, held on Monday evenings throughout August at around 9:30pm.

events.name: SandWorld Sand Sculpture Festival
events.blurb: The UK's dedicated sand sculpture festival, set at Lodmoor Park minutes from Weymouth Beach, where international artists create large-scale sculptures from sand and water on a new theme each year. Weymouth has a sand-sculpting heritage dating back over a century.

events.name: Dorset Seafood Festival
events.blurb: Held on Weymouth Harbour beside the beach, this is one of the UK's largest seafood festivals, featuring local seafood, food stalls and live performances on the waterfront.

events.name: Wessex Folk Festival
events.blurb: One of Britain's largest free folk festivals, held harbour-side in Weymouth with stages, ceilidhs and crafts close to the seafront.

events.name: Love Trails Festival
events.blurb: An outdoor festival combining trail running, hiking, adventure activities (surfing, coasteering, kayaking) and live music on the north Gower coast. Running routes wind through the villages of Llangennith and Llanmadoc, the gateway village to Whiteford Sands.

events.name: Gower Folk Festival
events.blurb: A small, volunteer-run folk music festival held at Weobley Castle Farm on the tidal salt marshes of north Gower, with concerts, workshops, a European dance evening and family craft activities. It takes place on the second weekend of June.

events.name: The Gower Festival
events.blurb: A fortnight of classical and chamber music featuring internationally acclaimed musicians performing in the historic churches and intimate venues across the Gower Peninsula, including St Cenydd's Church in nearby Llangennith.

events.name: Ras Dewi Sant (St Davids Marathon, Half Marathon & 10K)
events.blurb: A flagship running event based in St Davids with marathon, half marathon and 10K distances, starting at the Bishop's Palace and following country roads and the Pembrokeshire Coast Path near Whitesands Bay.

events.name: St David's Day Parade (Dragon Parade)
events.blurb: An annual parade in St Davids marking the patron saint's day, filling the city's main street with schoolchildren, community groups, music and creativity. A pilgrimage walk to the cathedral also takes place.

events.name: St Davids Cathedral Festival
events.blurb: A classical and choral music festival held in St Davids Cathedral, bringing renowned performers and emerging artists together for around ten days of concerts in the cathedral's acclaimed acoustic setting.

events.name: Surfing at Whitesands Bay (Porthmawr)
events.when: year-round, best surf in winter (often February)
events.blurb: Whitesands Bay is regarded as one of the best surfing beaches in Pembrokeshire, with surf schools and lessons running through the season and consistent clean waves most reliable in winter.
